notes.title: More lobby options, vote history window and rebalancing changes! (1.4.2)
notes.content:
UPDATE 1.4.2

[h2][b]FEATURES:[/b][/h2]

[h3]Vote History tab[/h3]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/I6k7uC5.png[/img]
[list]
[*] It is now possible to view the vote of each player on a specific Commissariat Proposal.
[/list]
[h3]Tyrant Special Permit Self Assignment option[/h3]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/nDhlhBc.png[/img]
[list]
[*] By default, the Tyrant used to be allowed to assign Special Permit to themselves. Some players have expressed frustration with this, therefore it is now possible to customize your match accordingly.
[/list]
[h3]7+ player two-sabotage requirement option[/h3]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/sECnPIH.png[/img]
[list]
[*] Same goes for the two-sabotage requirement on the 4th task when playing with 7+ players. The 4th task required two sabotages by two different dissident members to be sabotaged successfully. This is now customizable.
[/list]
[h2][b]REBALANCING:[/b][/h2]

[h3]Rebalancing Instability[/h3]
Instability is an important aspect of the game: it prevents players from indefinetely rejecting Commissariat Proposals, which would give Loyalists too much of a safe haven to fall back onto whenever they'd be undecided on the identity of other players.
By default the instability bar has 5 levels, triggering an instant Dissident win whenever this reached the maximum level.

This, however, created a [b]fatal flaw[/b]: on five players, whenever the player coming right after the Tyrant's turn held the [i]Commissar Role[/i], Loyalists could just reject [i]Commissariat Proposals[/i] enough times for the [i]Commissar Role[/i] to go back to the Tyrant. 
On five players, the maximum number of people that can be involved in a Decree is two. Therefore, this could be exploited to ensure the Loyalists always had a Decree involving the Tyrant (who is sure to be on the Loyalist side) enacting the decree: if it got sabotaged, it meant the other player involved was surely a Dissident.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/nQOODqc.png[/img]

The issue has been solved now, with the maximum instability level set to 4 for five players.

[h2][b]BUGFIXES:[/b][/h2]
[list]
[*] Network stability issues.
[/list]

notes.title: Patch notes for v1.4.1
Viva la Purgación!
notes.content:
[h1]Viva La Purgación![/h1]
After MONTHS of no updates, we're back with something big. We've pretty much added all of the features we intended to add from the release. Today we're proud to announce the [i]Viva La Purgación![/i] update, which adds new character models to unlock, a shop, an inventory for customization, a new scenario, two new soundtracks, a couple of Quality of Life improvements and solves some known bugs.

Let's start with the new features.



[h2]New Scenario (+new Soundtracks)[/h2]
Avena Club, a tropically inspired club.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/L2hoZZG.png[/img]
It is possible to choose the preferred Scenario in the Lobby Creation menu:

[img]https://i.imgur.com/kslrikf.png[/img]



[h2]Shop and Inventory (+new Character Models)[/h2]
You can now earn Loyalty Points by completing matches (not necessarily winning them). They can be spent in the Shop section of the game, where you can find loads of new Character Models that can be assigned to their respective character.

In addition, some tropically inspired characters from [i]Viva La Purgación![/i] Pack have been added, along with new emotes.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/HTYjhCQ.png[/img]
They can be equipped and unequipped in the Inventory Section of the game, where you will have the full list of Characters and Emotes that you possess.

They're Steam items! That means you can check them out in your Steam Inventory as well.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/XEpUzqD.png[/img]
Loyalty Points are also Steam Items.



[h2]Passworded Lobbies[/h2]
You can now add a password to your lobbies. These will still appear in the list of available lobbies if the [i]Hidden[/i] option is not selected, however they will now require a password.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/Gwo3fqS.png[/img]



[h3]Tweaks and Bugfixes[/h3]
Of course we've also solved some annoying bugs:
[list]
[*]Colour of the Table is now relative to the selected scenario.
[*]Written Text will no longer go out of bounds.
[*]Fixed a bug that would not let the screen resolution be set to 1440p.
[*]GOAT CRASH: fixed a bug that would crash the game if the player wrote their text overly out of bounds in the Journal.
[*]Fixed a bug that would sometimes not show the Journals of other players at the end of the game.
[*]Network and stability issues improvement.
[/list]

[h3]Known Bugs[/h3]
Ralph and I are constantly monitoring our Community Discord. We are currently investigating most of the bug reports that have been sent by you in the #report-a-bug channel. The following is a list of known bugs:

[list]
[*]Nameplate, Journal and Party Membership card [b]spawning away from the table[/b]. This seems to happen when the player focuses out of the game (minimizes the game in the toolbar) whilst the match is in the loading screen (the Waiting for Players screen) at the start of a game.
[*]The Tyrant sometimes [b]spawns either as a Dissident or a Loyalist[/b], forcing the players to recreate the match.
[*]The game status in the top left corner of the screen sometimes reports a [b]negative number[/b] of decrees remaining. 
[*]The "Form a Commissariat" dossier sometimes asks for a [b]negative number[/b] of players to be selected.
[/list]



[h2]A big thank you to everyone who plays The Purge Dilemma![/h2]

[b]If you encounter any bugs or wish to look for people to play the game with, join our [url=https://discord.gg/9fSwQkwbtx]Discord Community[/url]![/b]

[b]Remember that leaving a review for the game will greatly help the shaping of a solid playerbase.[/b]

[b][i]Thank you![/i][/b]

[b][h1]Achievement and Stats![/h1][/b]
Well, after a few weeks of no updates, we're back with something. First of all, a big thank you to the Community that continues to help the game grow and develop, both by joining our Community Discord to interact with other players and those of you who continue reporting bugs so that we are able to improve every aspect of the game and therefore your experience.

We got them working, finally. Both achievements and player statistics have been added to the game! Check this out.
[list]
[*] [h3]Steam Achievements.[/h3]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/9AQp0zt.png[/img]
Finally you can reach goals by completing these achievements!

[*] [h3]Player Stats[/h3]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/dzzgQwK.png[/img]
A Player Statistics section that shows how much you have done so far, from how many Dissidents you purged, to how many times you died.
[/list]

[h2][b]Tweaks[/b][/h2]
Some aspects of the game have also been tweaked:
[list]
[*] Added minimum time to each countdown adjustment in the Lobby settings.
[*] Resolved some network stability issues.
[/list]

[h2][b]Bugfixes[/b][/h2]
And of course, with the Major Update, comes some pretty significant bugfixing. We managed to get rid of some of the most known and reported bugs. The list is below:
[list]
[*] "Doppelganger" bug is now fixed. No longer will two players have the same character.
[*] "Democracy" bug is now fixed. No longer will the Tyrant sit among the other players.
[*] Fixed a bug where the match would become heavily unstable if one of the countdown was set to 0 (or other low values) in the Lobby settings.
[/list]

[url=https://discord.gg/TdaXvvBqKD][img]https://i.imgur.com/iG4x1yL.png[/img][/url]

[list]
[*] Fixed a bug where the Journal would not show the correct amount of Dissidents.
[*] Fixed a bug where any cooldown timer modification in the Lobby Options would not match the one in-game.
[*] Fixed a bug that caused the game to not proceed and be stuck even if all players had interacted with the Dossier.
[*] Fixed several bugs related to players leaving in the middle of the match during crucial phases.

[b]Known Bugs:[/b]
[list]
[*] Doppelgangers. There are times in which multiple players have the same character. The game is still able to proceed, however it might cause confusion. We're currently looking to fix this. notes.title: Redesigning The Purge Dilemma - Part 2
notes.content:
[h2]Welcome back![/h2]
Last time we gave a look at the design and model changes. However, we also pointed out that the game has been completely rewritten gameplay-wise.

As specified in the last Update, after a series of playtests we have uncovered many inconsistencies in terms of gameplay, from unbalanced mechanics all the way to non-engaging features. 

This is what we will focus on in this developer update. We will analyse a match in order, going from start to finish. Keep in mind that the screenshots you see in this developer update are taken across several different playthroughs, so they do not always refer to the same match. In addition, all design choices in the UI may still be subject to changes.

[h1]The Commissariat[/h1]
[b]The Commissariat[/b] is the new major gameplay addition. A group of players will be chosen to decide on a Decree, then everybody together will either vote in favour of the proposed Commissariat or not.

[h3]The Commissar[/h3]
[b]The Commissar[/b] role is assigned by the Tyrant at the beginning of the game...

[img]https://i.imgur.com/FuKDtNb.png[/img]

...and passed onto the next person (directly to their right) once every Decree has been completed.

The player currently holding the Commissar role will have to pick between the other players those that he wishes to involve in the next Decree...

[img]https://i.imgur.com/NeNn0Hg.png[/img]

...and then all the players, including the Tyrant and the Commissar, will vote in favour or against. The majority wins.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/TSqvJsh.png[/img]

[img]https://i.imgur.com/owdjuKa.png[/img]

Keep in mind that rejecting a Commissariat fills up the [b]Instability[/b] bar.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/2Q2VIeT.png[/img]

If it reaches five, it's game over for the Loyalists.



[h1]Decrees[/h1]
[b]The Decrees[/b] come in to replace what were previously known as Tasks.
When the Commissariat is proposed and everybody votes in favour, it will move onto the next step: the Decree. 

Every person that is part of the passed Commissariat (Commissar included) will then have to act on the Decree.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/z7NBQak.png[/img]

...with the ability to sabotage if you are a Dissident.

Supporting a Decree will shift the Paranoia in favour of the Loyalists (left), whereas Saboutaging will shift it in favour of the Dissidents (right).

[img]https://i.imgur.com/Pq2lnMB.png[/img]



[h1]Special Permits[/h1]
[b]Special Permits[/b] are your means to twist a game. They are assigned by the Tyrant upon reaching a certain stage on the Paranoia bar. 

[img]https://i.imgur.com/4buzzQD.png[/img]

A Tyrant may only assign one Special Permit per player, including themselves.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/jQ9YHCZ.png[/img]

[img]https://i.imgur.com/ai0iDxd.png[/img]

The player that receives the special permit will then be able to use it on another player. Above is an example of the Special Permit [b]Confidence[/b] which allows a player to show their identity to someone else.



[h1]Discussion Time[/h1]
The [b]Discussion Time[/b] remains unchanged. It's the time of the match in which players must sit down and talk among themselves, discussing what has happened in the previous Decree (if necessary) and share any vital information they possess, to try and somewhat gain a picture of who the Dissidents might be.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/6tEKxiG.png[/img]



[h1][b]Winning and losing[/b][/h1]
Although we plan on making it an adjustable parameter, five are the total Decrees on which players will work on. The Loyalists must Support three Decrees and the Dissidents must Sabotage three. The first team to achieve their goal wins, and their victory displayed in the ending screen.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/Ra5fWyf.png[/img]

[h3]The Purge (hidden chance)[/h3]
There is a case in particular in which Dissidents manage to Sabotage three Decrees immediately without the Loyalists ever Supporting a Decree, triggering [b]The Purge[/b].

[img]https://i.imgur.com/YhkUNxb.png[/img]

[img]https://i.imgur.com/8yubb8b.png[/img]

[img]https://i.imgur.com/G65KzZ4.png[/img]

In this case the Tyrant is given the opportunity to play their cards right, attempting through gathered information to pick the exact Dissidents among the players. If all Dissidents are purged then the Loyalists win.

[b]The host may disable this feature for their match in the Lobby creation menu:[/b]

[img]https://i.imgur.com/W3shTEw.png[/img]



[b]A reminder to everyone that the game will be available to play the next Steamfest in June 2023![/b]



[b][h2]Thank you for reading this Developer Update. See you in the next one![/h2][/b]

Make sure to follow us on Social Media! You can find us on:

notes.title: The Purge Dilemma - Progress Update 30/09/2022
notes.content:
[h3][b]Hello and welcome to our first Progress Update for the Purge Dilemma![/b][/h3]

The game has been in development for over a year now - although the Steam page was only created a few months back. We've done three Developer Updates so far, going over the roles of the game.

We're here to announce that we have prepared three videos, each explains every single role in less than two minutes and goes over the features, explaining all you can do including a few tips and tricks.

We are also currently working on a new trailer. We intend to refurbish the previous one: the camera angles, the background, the content... they weren't really as explanative as we would've hoped.

As for the game itself, we have completely restructured the default level, adding more props and more references to a tyrannical regime. It now actually feels like a Dacha - plus we got rid of the red table. Now it's a regular table.

And if you don't like the current map, you're probably going to feel relieved after I tell you that we are currently implementing a customization mechanic, that allows players to customize each character in The Purge Dilemma through items which will go in your Steam Inventory and will randomly be dropped as a result of playing. But most importantly, we intend to create new levels - new maps, which means new scenarios that allow the Purge to shift away from the default Dacha room. New maps with new themes, from all over the world.

notes.title: Developer Update #3 - The Purge
notes.content:
[h2]Hello and welcome to the third Developer Update for The Purge Dilemma![/h2]

In this Developer Update we will talk about the end-game phase which we call [b]The Purge[/b].

In the last Developer Update we mentioned the Paranoia system, but we didn't really go into detail as to not end up mixing several things together which could've easily confused players.

[b][h3]What purpose does the Paranoia serve in this social-deduction game?[/h3][/b]
The Paranoia system undoubtedly lays the foundation for the entire game. 

The Tyrant is a very paranoid character: he is afraid of those around him. He does not know who to trust in the Committee. He is sure that somebody is plotting against him and he must find out who. And he has to do so by avoiding killing innocent and loyal members of the Party.


[h3]The Paranoia Bar[/h3]
But when it comes to game mechanics, how does it influence the game?

It's pretty simple and very straightforward: The Tyrant's paranoia bar is visible on top of your nametag (it's the red one).

[img]https://i.imgur.com/TTPv1WF.png[/img]

The length of the Paranoia Bar is directly proportional to the number of players in a match.

As you complete tasks, you will notice that it will start filling up:
[list]
[*] Sabotaging a task will increase the Paranoia Bar by two points.
[*] Fulfilling a task will increase the Paranoia Bar by one point.
[/list]
Oh no, the Paranoia Bar has filled up! What happens now?

[h3]The last discussion[/h3]
When the Paranoia reaches its peak, you will have one final discussion time. The Tyrant player will have to wisely utilise the little time left. Discuss between players who you think the Dissents are, but be careful who you trust.

When discussion time is finished, The Tyrant will receive his final dossier.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/GkRzBMw.png[/img]

This is the most important dossier in the game. With this, the Tyrant will decide who will die... who shall be [b]purged[/b].

[u]The amount of people you can purge is equal to the number of dissidents there are in the match. The Tyrant player will have to accurately select the Dissidents based on his notes and his experience of the match. Leaving one Dissident alive will cause the entire Loyalist team to lose and the Dissident who remain alive will be the winners.[/u]

After selecting the players to purge, then [b]The Purge[/b] begins.

[h3]The Purge[/h3]
Eveything is dark. All you can do is look around - meet the gaze of your comrades, and pray that they will be shot instead of you.

All of a sudden you start hearing a shot after the other, as you notice Committee members slam their head into the table, lifeless.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/FMXe7QH.png[/img]

[b]And the game ends.[/b]
[list]
[*] If the Tyrant purges all the Dissidents, the Tyrant and the Loyalists win the match.
[*] If the Tyrant purges all but one Dissidents, then that Dissident will win the match.
[/list]

Dissidents don't all win together. Only those that stay alive will appear in the scoreboard.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/d37fYPb.png[/img]

When you press Continue, you will see how the game judges other players based on what they have done.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/dVC7LB7.png[/img] [img]https://i.imgur.com/irZSY5d.png[/img]

[i]The scoreboard and the player performance screens are still WIP[/i].

[b][h2]Thank you for reading this Developer Update. See you in the next one![/h2][/b]

Make sure to follow us on Social Media! You can find us on:

notes.title: Developer Update #2 - informant & Forger
notes.content:
[h2]Hello and welcome in the second Developer Update for The Purge Dilemma![/h2]

In this Developer Update we will talk about two subroles: the [b]Informant[/b] and the [b]Forger.[/b]

Last time we explained how the Task system works and we mentioned certain [i]Effects[/i] that 4-player Tasks can have. Today we are going to talk about them.

[b]As usual, stick with us to the end to hear about how these features apply to 5-player matches.[/b]

[b]Why is there the need of "effects" in a social deduction game?[/b]
Effects aim to introduce factors that severely determine the direction a match goes in based on a player's intuition, skill and general investigative capabilities. That is why we have decided to add the ability for all players to take matter into their own hands.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/j3QdSUU.png[/img] [img]https://i.imgur.com/oZaZhwk.png[/img]

2 and 3-player tasks have no effects.

Every time a 4-players Task is successfully completed and discussion time is over, an informant and a forger will be chosen. The event will be announced in the Chat Log.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/pZgGaLr.png[/img]


[b][h3]Informant[/h3][/b]
The first time an informant has to be chosen, a random player in the Loyalist team will be picked. A player cannot be an informant two times in a row.

The informant will then open up a dossier...

[img]https://i.imgur.com/IpYRa8o.png[/img]

... in which they can choose which player to investigate. 

The informant has to pick their player based on their past interactions with them or other listening to testimonies by other players. The choice is completely free. However investigating the wrong person will much likely result in a wasted investigation, especially if said person's identity has been falsified, in that case it will also lead to the Tyrant player receiving the wrong information.


[b][h3]Forger[/h3][/b]
Just like the informant, the forger is picked randomly, and the same player cannot be a forger two times in a row. This time however, it is chosen from the Dissident team.

The chosen forger will also open up a dossier...

[img]https://i.imgur.com/QIwqTRf.png[/img]

... in which they can choose which player to investigate. 

The forger is an extremely useful role that however requires high intuition skills to be put to good use. The forger will have to guess which player the informant is going to investigate for that round. It can be done by picking a highly suspicious player targeted in the previous discussion breaks.

Forging is a useful tool. It could severely impact the course of the match. The forger may decide to shield a fellow dissident partner, falsify their own identity if they think their cover is at risk or even go as far as falsifying the identity of a Loyalist opponent.

[b]Keep in mind that an identity will only be falsified for that investigation phase.[/b]


[b][h3]Investigation result[/h3][/b]
When both the informant and forger have picked their targets (or the time has expired, in which case their targets are picked randomly), the Chat Log will announce who has been chosen.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/VPXINyR.png[/img]

(keep in mind that the names between the brackets are for testing purposes only, in the actual match Steam Names will be displayed).

But only the Tyrant player will receive information on the target's identity.

[b]The identity of the forger and the informant WILL REMAIN ANONYMOUS. Feel free to claim it was you. In the end it is the other player's choice whether to believe you or not. This is a social deduction game, creating chaos is the main point![/b]

[img]https://i.imgur.com/6MzIUn7.png[/img]

At this point, it is the Tyrant's player responsibility to either find the information [i]truthful[/i] or claim it has been [i]falsified[/i].


[b][h3]Tyrant Informant[/h3][/b]
The worst-case scenario for all dissidents is having the Tyrant as the informant.

[b]How does that happen?[/b]
If the dissident team decides to take it easy and go on without sabotaging any tasks, the Stability bar will start filling up.

The Stability bar is located right below the Paranoia bar ontop of your nametag...

[img]https://i.imgur.com/XA0nQs2.png[/img]

... we will talk about the Paranoia bar in another Developer Update. For now let's stick with the blue Stability bar.

The Stability bar is a feature which mainly exists to punish lazy dissidents who for some reason forgot that their job is to give the Tyrant a hard time.

If three tasks are fulfilled in a row, the Stability bar will fill completely and the event triggers. the Tyrant will be chosen as informant and oh boy... that's going to be a real pain for you dissidents!
The event will be announced in the Chat Log...

[img]https://i.imgur.com/4Q7M6vX.png[/img]

... and the Tyrant will be able to investigate somebody's identity the same way a regular Loyalist informant does. This time however the investigated player will not be shown in the Chat Log and there won't be a forger able to meddle with the information. As usual, only the Tyrant will receive a dossier showing the player's identity. This time however, there is no doubt the information is truthful.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

[h2][b]5-player rules - Informant and Forger[/b][/h2]
In the last developer update we have mentioned 4-player tasks not being available. This means that there will be no Informant & Forger mechanic in 5-player matches for game-balance reasons.

[b]However[/b] the Stability is always there, no matter how many players. This means that the Tyrant will always be able to become an informant. So do your jobs you lazy dissidents!


[b][h2]Thank you so much for reading this Developer Update. See you in the next one![/h2][/b]

Make sure to follow us on Social Media! You can find us on:
[url=https://discord.gg/TdaXvvBqKD]Discord[/url]

notes.title: Developer Update #1 - Tasks
notes.content:
[h3]Hello and welcome to the first of many developer updates for The Purge Dilemma![/h3]

In this Developer Update we will talk about the Task System and briefly explain all of its features.

The Task System is arguably the most important aspect, since it pretty much determines most of what makes the core loop of the game. Coming up with a functional and balanced system was not so easy and it took a lot of testing. What will be shown here is the result of weeks and weeks of testing, rewriting and balancing.

[b]Before getting to it there is something we must clear out.[/b]
Playing the game with just 5 players requires its own rules. These kind of adjustments are something you see often when it comes to board games, therefore I advise you to read the note at the end of the Developer Update that addresses the 5 player case.

[h3]The Commissar[/h3]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/MtlgeMp.png[/img]

What you're currently looking at is The Tyrant's Commissar selection dossier. At the beginning of the game a dossier will appear infront of the Tyrant, allowing him to choose who the next Commissar will be.
The red bar at the bottom is the timer: if the Tyrant doesn't pick the Commissar before it reaches the end, a Commissar will be randomly picked. This puts both pressure on the the Tyrant player and prevents any attempt at holding the game hostage.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/ArRIV1f.png[/img]

The Commissar will have a dossier infront of them appear after they have been chosen, with which they are able to pick a Task. A log will appear in the chat telling the players who was chosen as Commissar.
Between the brackets will be the player's Steam name.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/Yxt1djx.png[/img]

[h3]The Task[/h3]
In the dossier you will have to choose between two randomly picked Tasks. As you can see, from top to bottom, the Task contains the following information:
[list]
[*][i]A representative polaroid coherent with the title;[/i]
[*][i]The title;[/i]
[*][i]How many players will be involved in the Task, Commissar included;[/i]
[*][i]The effects the Task will have on the match. A window will appear if you hover over the box with your cursor explaining what that effect does.[/i]
[/list]
Once the Task has been selected, the Commissar will be able to either sabotage or fulfill the Task, a decision which will be based depending on their role. Right after picking an option the dossier will be passed directly to the player on the right, who will also be able to sabotage or fulfill the Task and so on until the maximum number of players required to partake in a Task has been reached.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/GVJHAtn.png[/img]

If a player has decided to sabotage the task, then the players on the right will receive a sabotaged Task and will not be able to sabotage or fulfill.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/aht2UNn.png[/img]

[h3]Discussion time![/h3]
Once the last player has performed the Task, [b]Discussion time[/b] begins. Voice chat and text chat is enabled. [b]Every[/b] player, including the Tyrant, will receive a dossier which tells if the Task has been successfully fulfilled or sabotaged.
[list]
[*]If a single player sabotaged the Task, then the Result is [b]sabotaged[/b].
[*]If everybody fulfilled the Task, then the Result is [b]fulfilled[/b]
[/list]

[img]https://i.imgur.com/5cq21Rv.png[/img]

Now comes the [b]Social Deduction[/b] part. If a Task has been sabotaged, the the Tyrant player must interrogate the Committee members involved in the previous task. Through their testimony, the Tyrant will need to discover who among them is the [b]Dissident[/b]. Everything can be noted down on a notepad on your right.
Discussion time will expire once a five minute timer on the Tyrant's Dossier will reach the end, or whenever they decide to click [b]End discussion[/b] at the bottom.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/BNYGnWK.png[/img]

The result of a Task is what directly interferes with the Tyrant's paranoia. 
[b]But we will talk about that in another Developer Update.[/b]
[b]Task effects will also be explained in another Developer Update.[/b]

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

[h2]Q&A (read, this is important!)[/h2]
[h3]How many tasks are there?[/h3]
As of now, there are exactly 22 tasks. Depending on the severity, 2-4 players will be required to perform the Task.
The number of tasks depends on how many players are in a match.
Tasks requiring 4 players will apply effects to the match.

Oh and you can run out of tasks. They are limited, meaning that if the players perform 4 player tasks one after the other, they will not appear anymore. This also applies to 2 and 3 player tasks.
The number of available tasks decreases or increases depending on how many players are in the match.

[h3]Can the Tyrant take part in Tasks?[/h3]
Nope. If a player has the Tyrant directly on his right, then the next player performing the Task will be the player on the Tyrant's right. The order in which Tasks are performed is counter-clockwise.

[h3]Does the Tyrant always decide who the Commissar will be?[/h3]
Nope. the Tyrant will only be able to pick the Commissar at the beginning of the match. After that, the next Commissar will be [b]the player immediately to the right of the last player involved in the previous task[/b].

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

[b][h2]IMPORTANT[/h2][/b]
Remember the warning at the beginning of the Developer Update? This is what we have to clear out:
as we said, playing the game with 5 players requires its own rules. So what will change?

A match with 5 players [b]will not have Tasks requiring 4 players[/b] and [b]Tasks are randomly selected as soon as the next Commissar is chosen.[/b]


[b][h2]Thank you so much for reading this Developer Update. See you in the next one![/h2][/b]
